newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk government braces for key military meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turk government braces for key military meeting.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government, fresh from a censure motion win, prepared on Wednesday for a crucial meeting later this week with the chiefs of the secularist military.

Tension is expected to be high at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council (NSC), attended by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, because of recent public squabbling between the generals and the Islamist wing of the coalition.
"The tension, or the events that have caused tension, will be discussed at the NSC," the Hurriyet daily quoted Erbakan aide Aydin Menderes as saying.
The armed forces have warned the coalition several times in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, hit back on Tuesday.
"What is most important is the people not the state. The state only exists to serve the people," he told a meeting of his Welfare Party.
"Who are you? You are only three percent, you have no right to speak," he said in reference to the secularist elite.
Erbakan, whose party won a narrow plurality of 21 percent in general elections in December, 1995, survived a challenge to his rule later in the day.
MPs voted 281 to 246 to reject two leftist bids to hold a ballot on bringing down the coalition for allegedly threatening the country's secular system.
But Welfare's Menderes warned that the opposition was waiting in the wings to do deals with the secularist coalition partner True Path Party.
He predicted, however, that Erbakan would assure the military on Friday that he was not bent on turning NATO member Turkey into a strict Islamic state.
